key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over years, acute exacerbations. LOCATION: Bilateral, diffuse. DURATION: Chronic with acute exacerbations lasting days to weeks. CHARACTER: Dyspnea, chest tightness, productive cough. AGGRAVATING: Infections, cold air, exertion, smoking. RELIEVING: Bronchodilators, oxygen, steroids, antibiotics. TIMING: Chronic baseline with acute worsening. SEVERITY: Moderate to severe (5-9/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Chronic productive cough, dyspnea, wheezing, barrel chest, clubbing, weight loss, fatigue. KEY POSITIVES: Smoking history, chronic cough, dyspnea, wheezing. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain (unless pneumothorax), no fever (unless infection).

red_flags: Inability to speak in full sentences
